main_body: Two stacked wooden crates. The upper-left crate is the largest volume, with a plank-striped lid on top and a dark front face with a diagonal brace.
top_band: At x=15, rows 1-8: light tan #b98a55 alternating with mid #99683a plank stripes, under a row-0 outline of #7a4f2d. This is a clear lid surface.
evidence: The column scan shows a light lid band (L about 113-146, rows 1-8), then an abrupt step to a very dark row 9 (L=44), then the front face at L=65 for rows 10-17. The top is several rows tall and clearly lighter than the front. The dark row under it works as the eave shadow, and the front carries a diagonal brace framed by dark inner edges, so it reads as inset. There is no separate lighter front-edge line, but the tone step and eave shadow make it read as a 3/4 crate rather than a front elevation with a hat. The lower-right crate has the same structure. No receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 colours per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. The lid has 3 tones in alternating stripes and the front has about 3 dark browns, which is shallow next to the 5-6 steps in the references. The outlines are tinted dark brown (only 12% neutral), so they are not a sticker-style black line. The front face is a large, nearly flat dark brown field with just a diagonal brace and no grain or speckle. Tile density is far below the references, so the piece would look thinner and flatter beside them.
